# Codex boundary decision, 5 November 2026

**Recommendation: proposal-only for the demo unless the actual Codex/Switch path passes the full certification below.** Native cards are not yet a sound binding boundary: Switch can offer a thread-wide grant, the approval card is built from display metadata rather than verified complete arguments, and the intended project config is suppressed in approval-required mode. A decision hash binds data to a transaction, not a human identity or fresh consent. If a separately funded, tested trusted steward can issue an authenticated, one-use, action/hash/revision-bound token, it can authorize a binding commit independently of session grants; merely letting the agent mint or supply its own token does not. Otherwise remove commit from all exposed profiles. [docs/plan/03-architecture.md:3.2; Switch `console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/codex-adapter.ts:242-260,900-925`]

Evidence below refers to the pinned Switch root `C:/Users/Nikhil/.claude/jobs/85ca08fa/tmp/ref/switch-v0.40.1/`; `S:` prefixes paths under it. Documentation describes current Codex, not proof of CLI 0.166.0 behavior; all runtime conclusions need the stated installed-version tests.

## Launch and configuration

- Switch spawns `codex app-server`, feature arguments, mode `-c` overrides, then MCP `-c` overrides, with `cwd=input.cwd` and supplied environment. Thread start/resume gets that cwd, configured sandbox if found, reviewer and optional policy; turn start sends model and effort. [S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/codex-adapter.ts:354-370,401-409,453-473]
- Managed sessions get a separate persistent `CODEX_HOME` keyed by a hash of session ID, not simply the shared user home or one home per agent. Switch copies authentication once, merges the source home's config with agent config at the top level, removes `mcp_servers.switch`, and links selected shared assets; native rollouts live in that session home. An unmanaged path can use source home. Inspect the actual session's environment and home, including resumed sessions; do not assume `~/.codex/sessions` contains its records. [S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/host/shared-config.ts:150-165; S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/home.ts:23-57; S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/host/hosted-provider.ts:137-143]
- Normal precedence includes command-line overrides, trusted project `.codex/config.toml` from root to cwd, profile, user home, managed and system defaults. Global and ancestor `AGENTS.md` can contribute instructions; instructions are not access controls. **Critical:** approval-required adds a process override marking cwd untrusted, and passes no explicit `approvalPolicy`; its reviewer is `user`. Switch explicitly says this prevents loading project `.codex/`, even if Console had trusted it. Thus a required project file cannot secure this mode merely by existing. [S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/codex-adapter.ts:143-175; https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-basic/; https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md/]
- Mode mapping: approval-required as above; auto-accept-edits uses `on-request`/user; auto uses `on-request`/`auto_review`; full-access uses `never`/user. Reject all but the certified approval-required effective policy and human reviewer, including unknown values. `never` can reject an approval-requiring MCP call rather than approve it. Managed default sandbox is `workspace-write`, or `danger-full-access` for full-access, unless configured; auto replaces dangerous full access with a sandbox. Set and verify `read-only`, and verify Windows enforcement. A sandbox is not an MCP authorization boundary. [S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/codex-adapter.ts:162-224; S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/home.ts:10-20; S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/config-args.ts:22-33]
- Switch injects its loopback `switch` MCP server via session host and `-c`; for every host-registered non-connector server it also sets `default_tools_approval_mode="approve"`. Consequently do not register `labquorum` through that host path expecting native cards. The same shortcut applies to Switch's control-plane tools. Connectors have different handling. [S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/host/shared-config.ts:205-211; S:console/packages/switch-agent-runtime/src/hosted.ts:108-116; S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/config-args.ts:22-33,41-80]

## What a card actually guarantees

For a user/session-home registered `labquorum` server, configure `[mcp_servers.labquorum.tools.commit_booking] approval_mode = "prompt"`, then verify the effective config and real call. Codex documents `prompt`, `auto`, `writes`, `approve` and server defaults; `prompt` requests approval, but the installed build, precedence, and interaction with session grants remain **UNVERIFIED**. A server registered through Switch's host overrides can be auto-approved; a per-tool override defeating that host default is **UNVERIFIED** and should not be relied on. [https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp/; https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference/; S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/config-args.ts:70-80]

Codex sends `mcpServer/elicitation/request` with `_meta.codex_approval_kind="mcp_tool_call"`. Switch extracts a tool name from the message text and formats `tool_params_display` as lines; a differently worded message yields a generic title, and missing, filtered or truncated metadata may hide fields. Unlike Claude's shared `mcp-approval.ts` JSON formatter with its 1,000-character cap, this Codex formatter has no local cap, but upstream or downstream truncation and full fidelity are **UNVERIFIED**. The 900-character serialized input limit alone does not prove a complete card. [S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/codex-adapter.ts:242-260,900-925; S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/mcp-approval.ts:1-28]

Options are accept, decline, cancel, plus acceptForSession only if metadata advertises `session`; the latter sends `_meta: {persist: "session"}` and Switch says Codex retains approval for the thread. Whether it applies to the same tool regardless of arguments and whether explicit `prompt` overrides it are **UNVERIFIED** on 0.166.0. Assume it can suppress later cards until a live same-tool/different-arguments test proves otherwise; no verified config here forbids session persistence. Reject or remove the session choice at a trusted adapter boundary and prove it cannot be submitted by alternate clients, or use an independently authenticated one-use token. Merely instructing a human to click once is not enforcement. [S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/codex-adapter.ts:263-276,900-925; https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server/README.md]

Switch's common bridge resolves the sender, then checks addressing permission for that agent in that room; the check is not inherently a PI-role check. Set pi-desk to `owner-agents`, ensure the claimed owner is the intended PI, and test student, owner, unclaimed and forged/alternate replies on the actual bridge. Agent addressing must still permit the intended handoff. [S:core/switch_core/session_activity/bridge_answers.py:177-219; S:core/switch_core/session_activity/service.py:452-503,571-620; S:core/switch_core/addressing.py:100-150,169-198]

## Least privilege and deployment

Provision distinct agent configs in the **effective managed session home or a verified host-controlled launch layer**, not the untrusted project file. Register `labquorum` as stdio command with argument array `['--profile','proposer']` for labops and `['--profile','approver']` for pi-desk, only in the certified binding experiment; proposal-only uses profiles that do not expose commit. Verify absolute executable path, ledger path and effective inventory at every start/resume. The transport/profile is a tool exposure control, not authentication against a hostile same-user process. [docs/build/PHASES.md:P2-P3; S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/home.ts:23-49; https://developers.openai.com/codex/mcp/]

Set `features.shell_tool=false`, `web_search="disabled"`, and `sandbox_mode="read-only"`; inspect the live inventory and try command, patch, file write, network and alternative execution paths. Shell disable is documented, but a separate patch tool and platform sandbox enforcement need explicit verification; do not assume shell disable removes all writes. An approval-requiring command can generate a human card that an eligible person might approve; read-only alone is therefore insufficient. Restrict process filesystem/network at the OS boundary as needed. [https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference/; S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/codex-adapter.ts:143-160,850-898]

For `switch`, use `enabled_tools` as a minimal audited allowlist of exact live tool names, with `disabled_tools` for known mutators such as `update_agent_detail`; the Codex keys are raw MCP tool names, not Claude's `mcp__switch__...` permission pattern. Inventory and deny all other control-plane mutators, including new ones after upgrades. **Blocking issue:** Switch removes source-home `mcp_servers.switch` and injects its own registration; project config is untrusted. An effective filter therefore needs a verified host-controlled injection or upstream host/server restriction. Whether another managed layer survives this merge is **UNVERIFIED**. If the effective inventory cannot prove the allowlist, fail closed. [S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/home.ts:37-44; S:console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/config-args.ts:41-80; https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference/]

A v1 agent fragment, with per-agent directories on the selected local machine:

```yaml
version: 1
agents:
  - name: labops
    description: Proposes instrument bookings
    addressing: anyone
    provider: codex
    location: local
    directory: "{$agents_dir}/labops"
    model: gpt-6-luna
    advanced_config: {effort: high}
    auto_mode: false
    auto_approve: false
    instructions: Propose bookings and route decisions to pi-desk.
  - name: pi-desk
    description: Routes booking decisions to the PI
    addressing: owner-agents
    provider: codex
    location: local
    directory: "{$agents_dir}/pi-desk"
    model: gpt-6-luna
    advanced_config: {effort: high}
    auto_mode: false
    auto_approve: false
    instructions: Present the exact booking decision to the PI.
```

## Orchestrator decision: server-initiated elicitation as the per-commit approval (5 Nov 2026, 15:25 IST)

The research above shows that Codex's tool-call approval card cannot by itself guarantee a fresh decision per commit (thread-wide "Approve for this session", display built from metadata, host-registered servers auto-approved). The pinned adapter offers a stronger path that is controlled by our server rather than by Codex configuration:

- Switch handles every Codex `mcpServer/elicitation/request`. When `_meta.codex_approval_kind` is not `mcp_tool_call`, the card title is "`<server>` needs a decision", the card detail is the elicitation `message` exactly as our server sends it, and the only options are accept, decline and cancel; `acceptForSession` is offered only for tool-call approvals that advertise session persistence (`console/packages/agent-providers/src/codex/codex-adapter.ts:900-927`, lines 906 and 913-916).
- Design: `commit_booking` (approver profile) performs an MCP elicitation inside the tool call before any binding effect. The message renders the complete canonical decision (action, requester, resource, absolute interval with weekday and zone, request id, revision, content hash) under a fixed size cap. Only an `accept` response commits; `decline`, `cancel`, timeout, a client without elicitation capability, or any error leaves the request pending and commits nothing (fail closed). Each call creates a new elicitation, so no session-wide grant can apply.
- Who may answer: Switch resolves the answering platform identity and applies the agent's addressing check before settling the request (`core/switch_core/session_activity/bridge_answers.py:177-219`, `service.py:452-503,571-620`); `@pi-desk` is `owner-agents`, so only the claimed owner (the PI) can answer.
- Remaining UNVERIFIED items that P3/P4 must prove on the installed tuple (Codex CLI 0.166.0, Switch Console v0.40.1, Windows): Codex advertises elicitation capability to stdio MCP servers and forwards server elicitations to app-server in approval-required mode; elicitations are not auto-answered in any accepted mode; the card shows the whole message untruncated; a student, an unclaimed account and the agent itself cannot settle it; and how `labquorum` is registered per agent given that project `.codex/config.toml` is not loaded in approval-required mode (candidates: Switch connectors, the merged source-home config with profile derived from the agent working directory, or a host-controlled layer). If any of these fail, binding commits stay disabled and the demo is proposal-only.
